prior_decision.quote: Summarizing, these results are in line with those of the UK study about anxiety, depression, and traumatic stress [19]. The UK and Italian data identify factors associated with worst psychological health: being a woman, younger age, having children, preexisting health issues of self or someone close, and the moderate to high perceived risk of contracting COVID-19 within one month. Unlike Italy, in the UK lower household incomes and having (had) the COVID-19 were associated with worst psychological health outcomes.
prior_decision.location: Discussion, line 49 (see also Aims, line 14; Analytic Methods, line 34; Discussion, line 44; References, line 288)
prior_decision.reason: Omitted target. The paper explicitly re-tests two distinct UK C19PRC empirical papers [19,20]. In Section 3.2 (line 34, 41) and the Discussion (line 44: 'In a second part of the analysis, we replicated the approach by Shevlin et al. [19]'), the authors replicate the three binary logistic regression models from Shevlin et al. (2020) [19] (10.1192/bjo.2020.109) in the Italian sample and report mixed results (line 49: several risk factors matched the UK study, whereas lower household income and having had COVID-19 were associated with worse outcomes in the UK unlike Italy). Because [19] is an independent published paper whose findings are directly re-tested, it must be coded as a separate replication target.

luna_triage.reason: The Italian study explicitly conducts the second analysis by replicating Shevlin et al. [19], and its Discussion compares the Italian findings with that UK study. This is the distinct 2020 paper identified in the target (DOI 10.1192/bjo.2020.109); supplied row 259 is another Shevlin et al. 2020 paper with a different title and DOI (10.1111/bjhp.12430), cited separately as [20], so it does not represent [19]. The prior Argon objection agrees that [19] is a separate retested publication.
